title: The People of the Land
lead: 'Am ha'arets, "the people of the land," is a phrase with different meanings in different books: free landowning citizens in Kings, the non-exiled neighbors in Ezra, the common people in Ezekiel, and the community Haggai calls to work.

sections.h: Who are the people of the land?
sections.b: In 2 Kings 11 they are the landowning citizens who install Joash and kill Athaliah; in 2 Kings 21:24 they put Josiah on the throne. In Ezra 4:4 the people of the land discourage and frighten the builders. Ezekiel uses it of the nation or its landowners (Ezekiel 7:27; 22:29). Haggai uses it positively of those who are to work on the Temple (Haggai 2:4). Scholars debate whether it is a fixed legal class or a loose term.
